name: Change Request Form
one_liner: The one-page form that turns a request into a traceable project change.
purpose: The template states its own purpose: to capture the need and characteristics of a project change request. It is the first step of the change request process — once the change request is logged into the Change Log, the form is updated with the assigned Change ID and archived. The Guide adds that a change request logs an appeal to amend an agreed baseline: scope, requirements, deliverables, resources, costs, timeframe or quality characteristics.
created_in: Monitor & Control — Manage Project Change; changes can be raised in any phase by any stakeholder
approved_by: Project Owner (PO) and/or Project Steering Committee (PSC) approve or reject, per the project's escalation procedure
inputs: Project Change Management Plan (or Project Handbook)

lifecycle.what: Change process and this form defined in the plan
Tracked to closure through the Change Log
Archived; scope changes evaluated in the Project-End Report

fields.what: Cover block naming the owning organisation and department, with the document title and logo.
fields.castor: European Stability Mechanism — Lending Operations Division

fields.what: Date the form was issued and its version, so successive re-assessments of the same request are distinguishable.
fields.castor: Date: 12 Mar 2027 · Doc. Version: 1.1 (v1.0 12 Mar, v1.1 after impact assessment 19 Mar)

fields.what: Which project the change is aimed at — a change request always attaches to one project baseline.
fields.castor: Project CASTOR — Renewal of the Lending Operations System (LOS), ID ESM-2026-014

fields.f: Change ID: <link to the change log>
fields.what: The identifier assigned when the request is logged. The template says the form is updated with the assigned Change ID and then archived.
fields.who: PM assigns from the Change Log

fields.what: Short name of the change, used from here on in the Change Log and every Status Report.
fields.castor: Add SRF common-backstop screens to Release 2

fields.what: When the need was identified — not when it was approved. Fixes the age of the request.
fields.castor: 12/03/2027 (verbal request received 09 Mar 2027; put in writing 12 Mar)

fields.f: Requested by: <The name of the requestor/group>
fields.what: The person or group asking. Any project stakeholder may raise a change at any point in the lifecycle.
fields.castor: Cabinet of a Board of Directors member, relayed through PO Florence Nightingale

fields.what: The kind of change — which part of the baseline it touches: scope, requirements, schedule, cost, quality, resources.

fields.f: Priority: Very High / High / Medium / Low / Very Low
fields.what: Five-point priority, ticked on the form. Used to sequence this request against the other open ones.
fields.castor: Medium — the underlying instrument is not yet live

fields.what: Describe the current situation — a problem, an opportunity or a new need. Why is there a need for a change in the project?
fields.castor: Release 2 covers the live toolkit only; the common backstop to the Single Resolution Fund has no screens and no configured product.

fields.what: Describe the desired situation. What is the goal and benefits of this change request?
fields.castor: Backstop drawdown, monitoring and repayment screens delivered inside Release 2, ready on ratification day.

fields.what: The impact or risks of NOT implementing this change; quantify where possible to support cost-benefit analysis, the decision and the priority.
fields.who: PM with PCT · BM validates business impact
fields.castor: If not done, backstop onboarding relies on the configuration engine — SC3 target 6 weeks, which the PSC judged sufficient.

fields.what: Clarify what is out of the scope of this change request, so only the needed change is implemented and the boundary is explicit.
fields.castor: No change to collateral, pricing or the ESM Treaty-driven legal texts; no new reporting to the Board of Governors.

fields.what: Title and storage location of anything the assessor needs — impact assessment, minutes, requirement extracts.
fields.castor: CR-007 Impact Assessment v1.0, 19 Mar 2027 · MoM PSC 26 Mar 2027 · U:\CASTOR\05_Changes\

fields.f: Impact assessment (produced under step 2, recorded in the Change Log — not a field on this form)
fields.what: Assess whether it is really a project change, the impact of not doing it, its size against objectives, schedule, cost and effort, and its priority.
fields.who: PM with PCT estimates · SP confirms feasibility
fields.castor: 145 PD (Levallois 96 PD, ESM 49 PD), €392.000, +6 weeks on Release 2 — colliding with the parallel run

fields.f: Decision (recorded in the Change Log and Decision Log — not a field on this form)
fields.what: One of four outcomes: approve, reject, postpone or merge. Decision details are documented in the Change Log and communicated to the requestor.
fields.who: PO and/or PSC decide · PM communicates
fields.castor: PSC 26 Mar 2027, D-021: Postponed pending ESM Treaty reform ratification; re-assess within 30 days of entry into force

traps: No RASCI of its own: the Manage Project Change row governs (p.77) — PO=A, PM=R, PSC=C, BM=S.
'Impact or Risks' asks the impact of NOT implementing the change, not the cost of doing it.
The form carries no approval box: the decision lives in the Change Log, not on the form.
Four decisions exist — approve, reject, postpone, merge. Postponed is a real, correct outcome.
Change Status values: Submitted, Investigating, Waiting for approval, Approved, Rejected, Postponed, Merged, Implemented.

castor_excerpt.title: Extract — Change Request Form CR-007, Project CASTOR, 12 Mar 2027
rows: Project CASTOR — Renewal of the Lending Operations System (LOS)
Add SRF common-backstop screens to Release 2
12/03/2027 — request made verbally on 09 Mar 2027 by the cabinet of a Board of Directors member; PM required it in writing before any work started
Cabinet of a Board of Directors member, relayed through Project Owner Florence Nightingale

Release 2 delivers straight-through disbursement for the live toolkit — stability support loans, bank recapitalisation, PCCL/ECCL, PMSF and SMSF. The common backstop to the Single Resolution Fund has no dedicated screens and no configured product.
Backstop drawdown, monitoring and repayment screens built into Release 2 so that the instrument can be operated from day one of the ESM Treaty reform entering into force.

None on the live toolkit. The instrument-agnostic configuration engine already delivers success criterion SC3 — new instrument onboarding in 6 weeks instead of 9 months — so the backstop can be configured after ratification without code.
Collateral and pricing logic; ESM Treaty legal texts; any new reporting to the Board of Governors; changes to Release 1.
Impact assessment (19 Mar 2027, filed as reference)
145 PD — Levallois 96 PD, ESM 49 PD — and €392.000. Release 2 slips 6 weeks from 17 Dec 2027 to 28 Jan 2028, overlapping the parallel run that starts 08 Jan 2028.

Postponed. Ratification of the ESM Treaty reform is incomplete, so the backstop is a planned capability, not a live one. Re-assess within 30 days of entry into force. Change Log status set to Postponed; requestor informed by the PO.
